samples.summary: Markdown URL gate validates a WHATWG-normalized URL but emits the raw string: an href/src containing a tab or newline passes `isSafeUrl` and breaks out of the link destination, injecting arbitrary Markdown/raw HTML into the exported `.md`.
samples.evidence: `isSafeUrl(href)` (packages/core/src/url/index.ts:26) parses with `new URL(...)`, and the WHATWG URL parser removes every ASCII tab/LF/CR from the input before parsing. The value written to the file is the untouched `style.href` — `escapeMarkdownHref` (markdown.ts:296) escapes only `\` and `)`, not whitespace or control characters. Chain: an attacker-controlled document run carries `href = "https://example.com/\n\n"`. Nothing validates href on the way into the model — HTML paste copies the attribute verbatim (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:597-599, where ` ` in a pasted `` decodes to a real newline), as do DOCX import and a collaborator writing the CRDT directly. `new URL` strips the newlines, sees `https:`, so line 224 accepts it; line 225 then writes the raw newlines into the file, producing: [click](https://example.com/ ) The link syntax is terminated by the newline and the remainder becomes a top-level block. Any renderer of the exported file that permits raw HTML (marked's default, markdown-it with `html:true`, a docs-site build pipeline) executes it. Line 270 (`![alt](${escapeMarkdownHref(image.src)})`) has the identical hole on the `isSafeUrl(src)` branch; the `data:` branch is safe because `SAFE_IMAGE_DATA_URI` (line 247) is anchored and excludes whitespace. Note the serializer already escapes `<` in text runs (line 280), so the file otherwise treats raw-HTML injection as in scope. Fix: emit `new URL(href).href` (the string that was actually validated), or reject any href containing whitespace/C0 control characters before writing.

samples.summary: `EditorAPI.setPageSetup` writes caller-supplied geometry to the shared document with no validation; the only bounds check lives in the React dialog, and the pre-existing ruler path clamped its own values.
samples.evidence: `writePageSetup` calls `resolvePageSetup(setup)` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:751), which only shallow-copies — it does not clamp or reject. The other producer, the ruler drag, clamps margins to >= 0 itself (packages/docs/src/view/ruler/index.ts:402-405), and the new dialog does its own inch parsing and "room for content" check (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-page-setup-dialog.tsx). So the sole guard on the new public entry point is UI-side: any other holder of `EditorAPI` (it is exported from `@wafflebase/docs`) can write negative, `NaN`, or absurdly large margins/paper dimensions, and the value lands in the store and syncs to collaborators, who repaginate against it (packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:55-56 computes `contentHeight`/`availableWidth` with no floor). I could not build an infinite loop out of it — the table-split `while` at pagination.ts:116 still advances when `contentHeight <= 0` — so impact is layout corruption / oversized page allocation rather than a hang. Validation belongs on `writePageSetup`, the single documented write path, not on one caller.
searchedFor: grep resolvePageSetup / DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP / PAPER_SIZES in packages/docs/src/model/types.ts
read packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts lines 1-185 for contentWidth/contentHeight clamping
grep setPageSetup across the repo for other write paths

samples.summary: `safeFilename` extended to `md`/`txt` still does not strip a leading dot, C0 controls, or bidi overrides from the user-controlled document title used as the download filename.
samples.evidence: The sanitizer replaces only `[\\/:*?"<>|]`, so a title such as `".bashrc"` yields `.bashrc.md` (a dotfile) and a title containing U+202E can visually reverse the displayed extension in a file manager. Path separators are stripped, so no traversal — and both new extensions produce inert text, so impact is cosmetic. Pre-existing for the already-shipped `.pdf`/`.docx` and explicitly recorded as a known limitation in docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-surface-existing-features-todo.md; noted only because the signature is being widened here.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. markdown.ts:224-225 validates `style.href` with `isSafeUrl` but emits the untouched raw string through `escapeMarkdownHref` (markdown.ts:295-297), which escapes only `\` and `)`. `isSafeUrl` (packages/core/src/url/index.ts:24-31) is `new URL(href)` plus a protocol allowlist; the WHATWG basic URL parser strips ASCII tab/LF/CR from the input before parsing, so `https://example.com/\n\n` passes the gate while the normalized `url.href` is discarded. The newlines are then written verbatim, terminating the `[](...)` destination and emitting the remainder as a top-level block, which any renderer permitting raw HTML executes. markdown.ts:270 has the identical hole via the `isSafeUrl(src)` branch of `isSafeImageSrc` (line 251); the `data:` branch is genuinely safe (anchored regex, line 247). The input side is unguarded: clipboard.ts:596-601 and 698-703 assign `el.getAttribute('href')` verbatim (entity-decoded, so ` ` becomes a real newline), clipboard.ts:148-149 does the same for the JSON payload, and docs-tree.ts:116 / yorkie-doc-store.ts:187 copy the CRDT attribute straight into `style.href` — every `isSafeUrl` call in the repo is at render/export time, never on ingest, so no upstream guard makes this unreachable. The output reaches a real sink: cli/src/docs/content.ts:129, cli/src/slides/content.ts:184, frontend/src/app/docs/text-actions.ts:44. In lane as injection/unsafe input handling, and the serializer's own escaping of `<` in text runs (line 280) confirms raw-HTML injection is in this file's threat model — an added-but-bypassable gate.
